R2-01.why: Thumbstick + one contextual button and no aiming is solid, and 5-min rounds fit, but over-shoulder cameras in cluttered interiors are fiddly on phones, choosing a 'Hide here' hotspot by tapping glowing world points is a small-target task, and the Parent ends up with 5 buttons on the right edge.
R2-01.fix: Have the contextual button cycle through hotspots (or auto-pick the nearest valid one) rather than requiring world taps; use a top-down/elevated camera in PANIC; merge Parent gadgets into a radial on one button.

R2-02.why: Built for a phone: no thumbstick, one big HOLD plus one contextual verb, auto camera, server-predicted kinematic raft that runs fine on low-end devices, 3-4 min runs. Risks: with 6 seats your own seat is a small spot on screen, and timing a contextual verb you can't clearly read is frustrating.
R2-02.fix: Ring your own seat with a persistent coloured highlight and an icon above the verb button for the upcoming hazard; give each verb a generous timing window plus an audio cue.

R2-03.why: 'Release stick = freeze' is a great touch-native verb. But the Guard must aim the flashlight by camera-drag and tap-tag small statues among ~30 NPCs on a 6-inch screen, and the 0.3 s server grace will feel unfair on mobile latency.
R2-03.fix: Have the Guard tag with a centre-reticle TAG button (soft auto-lock to the statue in the cone) instead of world taps; scale freeze grace to measured ping; enlarge pose silhouettes.

R2-04.why: The rare concept whose core verb is native to touch (gesture runes), with no movement or camera, forgiving recognition and 6-8 min runs; PC is the adapted platform here, not mobile. Watch points: the finger hides enemies, full-screen drawing can trigger iOS/Android edge swipes, and fusion VFX may stall low-end devices.
R2-04.fix: Keep a 10% dead-zone at the screen edges and put enemy lanes in the top half so the thumb doesn't cover them; add a low-end VFX tier (fewer particles, reduced fusion effects).

R2-05.why: Tap item -> fullscreen inspect -> drag tool -> BUY/REJECT is a clean touch flow with no-text visual tells. But the forger's back-room swaps still need thumbstick navigation, the 'who touched what' evidence board for 4-8 players is icon-dense on a phone, and a fullscreen inspector hides what is happening in the shop.
R2-05.fix: Show the evidence board as one scrollable row per player with large portraits; add a mini 'activity ticker' during inspection; snap forger swaps to a contextual button at shelf hotspots.

R2-06.why: The core skill is spotting subtle anomalies (tints, small moves) in CCTV thumbnails, which is about the worst task for a 6-inch screen at low brightness; several live ViewportFrames/camera feeds are expensive on low-end devices; dim close-up horror is hard to read on phones.
R2-06.fix: Make anomalies bold and one per camera, show a single feed fullscreen with swipe to change camera instead of a grid, render feeds as server-swapped snapshots instead of live viewports, and add a brightness/visibility assist.

R2-07.why: No mobile controls are given. The core verb is framing ghosts with a held camera, so it needs two-thumb move+aim on touch, plus dark horror visuals; it reads as a PC Content Warning port. Generous auto-framing and the replay theatre help.
R2-07.fix: Add a 'lock-on film' button that auto-tracks the nearest ghost event while you only move; brighten the camera viewfinder (night-vision look); spell out a 3-button touch layout.

R2-08.why: Auto-grab and linked carry suit mobile and shifts are short, but the core skill is precise analog movement (don't run, don't turn sharply, navigate stairs/revolving doors) on Roblox's imprecise dynamic thumbstick; no mobile spec is given.
R2-08.fix: Add a 'Careful walk' toggle that caps speed and smooths turning, or make the parcel's stability depend on a hold-steady button instead of fine analog deflection; show a large turn-sharpness warning arc.

R2-09.why: Drag/tap on a 3x3 board, auto-place, one timed tap ability, no avatar or camera, 4-min matches: Clash Royale-style, designed for phones, and cheap to render. Only risks: tiny trait/mutation icons and readability when watching four boards plus gremlin hazards.
R2-09.fix: Show only your board plus the current opponent's (others as a mini HP strip); make the live-tap button large with a clear timing ring; use big silhouettes for mutations instead of small icons.

R2-10.why: UI-driven, tap-the-matching-stamp relay, pictographic manual, 60-90 s devices: strongly touch-friendly and cheap on low-end devices. The concern is fitting the device, the stamp wheel and the manual pages on one 6-inch screen, and some of the 25 modules may need small precise interactions.
R2-10.fix: Give each module a fullscreen zoom when tapped; dock the stamp wheel as a bottom-centre bar clear of the corners; keep module hit-targets at least 60 px and never use colour alone.

R2-11.why: Overcooked-style running between stations works on a thumbstick, but a crowded 6-player cabin causes camera occlusion and congestion, and dragging the yoke while flashing alerts cascade is busy on a phone; no explicit touch layout.
R2-11.fix: Use a fixed cutaway side or top camera of the cabin; add an auto-path 'go to station' tap on the flashing icons; one contextual USE button; give the pilot a large drag zone in the screen centre, clear of the corners.

R2-12.why: Thumbstick + HOLD SPRAY (auto-aim) + RESCUE with a fixed elevated wall-fading camera is a well-thought-out mobile layout and 5-min runs fit. But fire and smoke particles on a spreading grid are the biggest low-end performance risk in the set, and smoke that hides rooms hurts readability on small screens.
R2-12.fix: Render fire/smoke as grid-tile decals with capped particles (low-end tier), show critter locations as bold pulsing icons through smoke, and place SPRAY/RESCUE above the jump button, not in the corner.

overall_notes: Clear split: concepts that drop the avatar-move-plus-camera model (R2-04, R2-09, R2-02, R2-10) feel built for mobile; avatar-action concepts with auto-aim/contextual buttons (R2-01, R2-03, R2-05, R2-12) are solid adaptations; concepts whose core skill is visual subtlety or precise analog control (R2-06, R2-07, R2-08) or that leave out a mobile spec (R2-07, R2-08, R2-11) are PC-first. Recurring risks: dark horror visuals, particle-heavy VFX on low-end devices, Guard/Parent roles needing world-tap precision, and right-side button clutter near the default jump button.
